title: Design System: RAG Lab Wire Desk

display.purpose: The masthead only: 'RAG Lab' in chalk, 'Wire Desk' in paper. 2.2rem at 720px and below.

headline.purpose: Uppercase wire names, section heads, the hold stamp and gate verdicts, at copy size.

copy.purpose: Teletype: every filed piece, the answer galley, questions and hashes. Rank, slug and score at 700; section line italic.

body.purpose: The desk's own prose: lede, notes, status, footers. Tabular figures page-wide.

label.purpose: Uppercase keys: ASSIGNMENT, ledger keys, table headers, the Golden note key.

slug.purpose: The four-letter source code in white on its fixed source colour.

shadows.name: strip-on-desk
shadows.purpose: Teletype strips lifting off the desk.

shadows.name: slip-focus
shadows.purpose: The slip while its input has focus: a pencil ring.

shadows.name: stamp-double-rule
shadows.purpose: The inner paper gap and inner rule of the hold stamp; texture, not elevation.

motion.name: ease-desk
motion.purpose: The one easing: feed, pencil draw, button press.

motion.name: feed
motion.value: 340ms; clip-path inset(0 0 100% 0) to inset(0) with translateY(-6px) to none; delay wire*110ms + piece*55ms; fill backwards
motion.purpose: Copy feeds off the teletype when a story is filed.

motion.name: pencil-draw
motion.value: 550ms; stroke-dashoffset len to 0 via Web Animations API; delay 480ms + join*70ms; fill backwards, nothing held after the end
motion.purpose: Joins draw after the copy lands; the resting line is always visible.

motion.name: press
motion.purpose: File story and desk buttons on press.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: The resting state is shown directly.

breakpoints.name: stack
breakpoints.purpose: Wires, run and drawers stack; pencil layer removed; per-piece 'Editor ranked it #N' / 'Spiked' lines carry the joins.

breakpoints.name: narrow
breakpoints.purpose: Page padding 20px 16px; masthead stacks; slip takes its own row; sprocket margins 14px; ledger single-column; hash and misses columns hide.

narrative.overview:
A question is a story assignment on a newsroom wire desk. Three wires file at once: DENSE (meaning), BM25 (exact words), and between them THE EDITOR, the hybrid that merges the two by rank. Each wire's take arrives as a canary teletype strip with sprocket feed holes down both margins, lying on a dark green-black desk blotter. The editor works with a blue pencil: pencil lines join the same chunk across wires, ring the right copy, and write the fusion arithmetic under each merged piece. Copy the guard flagged gets a red HOLD FOR LEGAL rubber stamp and its text struck through; copy the editor did not run is marked spiked; every take ends with "— 30 —".

Density is a working desk's: three full columns of copy side by side, every piece carrying rank, source slug, score on its own scale, section and a clamped excerpt. There is one copy size. Rank is carried by weight, case, reversal (the first piece's rank is printed reversed, paper on ink) and rule (dashed rules between pieces, double rules between desk zones), never by a bigger font. Colour is material, not decoration: the desk, the paper, the ink, the pencil and the stamp each are a physical thing on a desk, and the six source slugs are fixed codes like a wire service's.

The world is its own: distinct from order-lab's split-flap departures board (black board, gold flap ink, condensed signage) and from mesh-lab's grey-blue bench instrument. It refuses the category default of a chat box with a sources panel and a metrics table.
keyCharacteristics: Canary paper strips (with sprocket margins) on a dark green-black desk; paper lifts off the desk, desk controls stay flat.
One type size (15px) for everything except the masthead; rank by weight, case, reversal and rule.
Courier Prime for all filed copy; Libre Franklin for the desk's own signage and prose.
Blue pencil is the editor's hand: joins, the right-copy ring, fusion sums, the one filled button.
Red is reserved for the hold stamp and failure; source colours are fixed per corpus file.
One motion moment: copy feeds in, then the pencil draws. The resting state is always fully visible.

rules.name: The Stamp Red Rule
rules.body: Red marks only the guard and failure: the HOLD FOR LEGAL stamp, the held strikethrough, the HELD ledger key, the failing gate, and error text. Never a brand colour, a highlight, or a warning that is merely waiting.

rules.name: The Two Pencils Rule
rules.body: The pencil is one colour in two tints: pencil on paper, pencil-desk on the desk. Never draw a paper-pencil line on the desk; it falls below a readable contrast.

rules.name: The Fixed Slug Rule
rules.body: Each corpus file keeps its colour and four-letter code everywhere it appears (wires, ledger, intake table). Never reassign or cycle source colours by position.

rules.name: The One Copy Size Rule
rules.body: Everything below the masthead is 15px. Hierarchy comes from weight (400/600/700/800), case and tracking, reversal (the first rank is paper on ink), italic for the section line, and rules. Never introduce a second text size to rank something.

rules.name: The Two Hands Rule
rules.body: Filed copy is Courier Prime; the desk's signage, controls and explanations are Libre Franklin. A string the retriever or answerer produced is typewriter; a string the page wrote to explain it is gothic.

rules.name: The Paper Lifts Rule
rules.body: Only paper casts a shadow. Anything made of the desk (buttons, toggles, tables, drawers) stays flat and is separated by desk-rule lines.

dos: Do keep every string below the masthead at 15px; rank with weight, case, reversal and rule.
Do set retrieved and answered text in Courier Prime and the page's own explanations in Libre Franklin.
Do show labels as `file#chunk` without ".md", identically on wires, galley and ledger.
Do use pencil-desk (not pencil) for any mark drawn on the dark desk.
Do label every score with its scale and keep each wire's decimals fixed (3, 4, 2).
Do replace pencil joins with each piece's "Editor ranked it #N" / "Spiked" line wherever the wires stack (1100px and below).
Do end motion on the visible resting state; never leave a mark that only appears through animation.
donts: Don't use red for anything except the hold stamp, held strikethrough, HELD key, gate failure and error text.
Don't reassign a source's colour or code, or give a new source a colour already taken.
Don't cast shadows from desk controls, tables or drawers; only paper lifts.
Don't let the stamp overlap copy; it sits in the flow above the struck text.
Don't collapse the three wires into a chat box with a sources panel and a metrics table.
Don't add a second text size to rank or emphasise something.
